Q: How to convert quadratic bezier curve code into cubic bezier curve? A:

If the original answer's animated diagram is difficult to understand, this is easier:

In a cubic Bézier curve, a linear interpolation is applied on each line segment connecting the four control points, producing three intermediate points.

Another interpolation is done on the line segments connecting the three intermediate points, producing a point on each.

Afterward, an interpolation between those two new points produces the curve point.

Q: http.sslVerify=false doesn't disable ssl verification in git config A:

Just to be sure: Did you perhaps have the GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY set in your user's environment that would override the corresponding global setting http.sslVerify?

Also, I'm not sure whether you should see a tailing slash '/' in reference 'https://githubserver.company.com/repository.git/'. Are you fetching the directory or the repo itself?

Most likely explanation is a broken certificate chain or missing trust.

Perhaps de HTTP proxy server somehow misbehaves are does not allow you to setup the secure connection. Does is support SSL/TLS and does your request run through the appropriate network ports? I'm curious whether you are able to do a (non-git) HTTPS downloads over proxy's from that same target server...

Q: Render HTML elements simultaneously A:
  • Give them visibility: hidden (or similar) initially and overwrite that using a tag that comes after them in the HTML code:
    • a <script> tag
    • or a <style> tag
    • or for example <span class="young-sibling"> that will trigger :has(+ .young-sibling) { visibility: visible; }
  • or create those elements programmatically in a single <script> instead of including them in the HTML code.

For elements such as <img> and <iframe>, you may additionally want to wait for the load event of each of them. For example, if you want to show such an element simultaneously with one that doesn't have a load event, you have to choose the option above of overwriting visiblity with <scipt> and wait both for that <scipt> to get reached as well as the load event to occur before making them visible.

Q: How do I code without being completely dependent on AI? A:

"it's OK to use AI while you are learning." - For the most part, I recommend against this. The problem is that our brains are super lazy, so the, "should this information be retained" algorithm in our brain tends to answer, "no" unless the information was a bit painful to obtain. The secondary problem is that cognitive offloading to external tools tends to increase dependence on those tools. To be clear, I'm not saying to avoid AI: I'm specifically saying that using AI is counterproductive to the goal of reducing dependence on AI.
